patches.value: Define U and μ as declared, and choose a nonempty finite list g of nonzero R-generators of J from F001; let k≥1 be its length, and write it g_1,...,g_k. For any rational q₀ and any finite R-linear combination Σ_(j=1)^k r_j g_j, tensor bilinearity gives q₀⊗Σ r_j g_j=Σ(q₀r_j)(1⊗g_j). Consequently the finite set {1⊗g_j:1≤j≤k} spans U over ℚ. Apply M008 with F=ℚ and A=U to this finite set; since the span is all of U, U is finite-dimensional. To check injectivity of μ, let s₀≥0 be arbitrary, take arbitrary families Q_1,...,Q_(s₀)∈ℚ and C_1,...,C_(s₀)∈J, and set z₀=Σ_(l=1)^(s₀)Q_l⊗C_l. Every element of the algebraic tensor product has such a finite-sum presentation. Define D to be the product of the positive denominators of the Q_l (the empty product is 1), and put H_l=D Q_l∈ℤ. Then D is a nonzero integer and tensor balancing over R, which contains ℤ, gives z₀=(1/D)⊗Σ H_l C_l. Temporarily assume L2: μ(z₀)=0. Its image is (1/D)Σ H_l C_l, so Σ H_l C_l=0 in ℂ, hence z₀=0 in U. Discharge L2. Since the finite presentation was arbitrary, the kernel of μ is zero, which proves injectivity by applying this to the difference of any two tensors with equal images. Its image is exactly span_ℚ J, since it consists of finite rational combinations of elements of J and contains them all.

patches.value: Define Θ:T→U^I by Θ(q₀⊗Σ c_i e_i)=(q₀⊗c_i)_i, and define Ψ in the reverse direction by summing the maps q₀⊗c↦q₀⊗(c e_i) on coordinates. The coordinate maps in F001 are R-linear, so these balanced maps extend to ℚ-linear maps of the indicated tensor products. The composites ΘΨ and ΨΘ are identities: on an elementary tensor in a single coordinate the first is that same coordinate tensor, and on q₀⊗z the second is q₀⊗Σ c_i e_i=q₀⊗z. Additivity and generation by pure tensors prove the identities everywhere. Therefore Θ is a linear equivalence. Set r_J=dim_ℚ U. By F002, U is finitely generated over ℚ, and M009 says it is free. With M010 supplying the strong rank condition for ℚ, apply M004 to the finite constant family U indexed by I; it gives dim_ℚ(U^I)=Σ_(i∈I)r_J=n r_J. Apply M005 to Θ and combine with F003 to obtain n=n r_J. Since n>0 by N001, integer arithmetic yields r_J=1.
For every q₀∈ℚ and c₀∈J define μ(q₀⊗c₀)=q₀c₀, extending by the tensor universal property from balanced multiplication.

By H001, an integer maps to zero in K exactly when divisible by p. Thus for arbitrary integers A₀,B₀ with B₀≠0 and p∤B₀, the fraction A₀/B₀∈R has a nonzero denominator image in K; and φ(A₀/B₀)=(A₀·1_K)(B₀·1_K)^(-1) is defined. Equality of fractions follows by cross multiplication, so the formula is well-defined and preserves addition, multiplication and 1. The same formula in F_p gives ψ:R→F_p. It is onto, since every integer residue occurs, and its kernel is pR: ψ(A₀/B₀)=0 is equivalent to p∣A₀, hence A₀/B₀=p((A₀/p)/B₀). Conversely multiples of p have zero image. The induced map R/pR→F_p is therefore a bijective ring map. Both constructions agree with the usual inclusion F_p→K. Every unit of R has nonzero image in K, since its image has a multiplicative inverse. In particular N002 shows that r! for 0≤r≤λ and binom(λ,j), j∈I, have nonzero images in K.
